greeting.title: Hi all, I'm Catalin
greeting.subtitle:
Analyzing what happens within systems, identifying threats, and helping defend against them: this is my work as a SOC Analyst.

My path began in software development and evolved into cybersecurity, with a degree in Computer Science and a Master in Cybersecurity. I combine an understanding of how applications work with an analytical approach to security, attention to detail, and curiosity about what lies behind an anomaly.

skills.area.monitoring.title: Monitoring and Offense analysis
skills.area.monitoring.desc: I investigate IBM QRadar Offenses by correlating events, sources, destinations, protocols, URLs, domains, and processes to understand the nature and impact of alerts.
skills.area.hunting.title: Threat Hunting
skills.area.hunting.desc: I investigate deviations from baseline: spikes in Firewall Deny and Permit events, quarantined IPs, and failed MyMail logins. I extend searches beyond individual Offenses, filtering by hosts, users, and time ranges.
skills.area.endpoint.title: Endpoint and email security
skills.area.endpoint.desc: I analyze processes, files, hashes, and suspicious behavior with Cynet EDR. Using Microsoft Defender, I investigate emails, URLs, and attachments for phishing, spam, and malware.
skills.area.network.title: Network and application security
skills.area.network.desc: I analyze WAF, firewall, proxy, and DNS events: SQL Injection, Path Traversal, Command Injection, web scanning, access to sensitive files, and communications with IOCs. I verify whether traffic was blocked, allowed, or quarantined.
skills.area.incidents.title: Triage and L1 incident handling
skills.area.incidents.desc: I collect evidence, correlate information from security systems, and assess events during initial triage. I prepare technical reports and escalate to higher tiers or relevant teams when needed.
skills.area.intelligence.title: CERT and Threat Intelligence
skills.area.intelligence.desc: I add and manage IOCs in MISP, including indicators from institutional CNAIPIC reports. I record and track MISP Sightings for indicators observed within the infrastructure.
skills.additional.title: Documentation and integrated monitoring
skills.additional.desc: I track security activities requested in the ECB context, maintaining documentation and evidence. Alongside cybersecurity work, I monitor physical security through PSIM, reviewing events and alarms from integrated systems.

buildweeks.title: Cybersecurity labs
buildweeks.intro: Three team projects completed during my training: from network design and vulnerability testing to threat analysis. Reports, code and evidence organised by Build Week.
buildweeks.indexNote: Each topic opens the PDF at the indicated page. On some devices you may need to select the page in your reader.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.title: Secure network & Python tools
buildweeks.buildweek-1.description: Team leader for a segmented business network project covering 120 hosts, with three Python tools to analyse HTTP services, TCP ports and network traffic.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.overview: I served as team leader for the Build Week project about the fictional Theta company. The team project combines a six-floor network, DMZ services and analysis tools. The collection includes the Packet Tracer topology, configuration report, cost estimate, slides, three documented scripts and lab logs.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.0: Segmentation with six VLANs, 802.1Q trunks, inter-VLAN routing and DHCP addressing.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.1: Definition of ACLs, firewall zones, NAS access and DMZ web server isolation.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.2: HTTP method analysis, TCP scanning and IPv4 traffic inspection with Python raw sockets.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.3: Log collection and technical documentation of network design decisions and test results.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.title: Black-box challenges & penetration testing
buildweeks.buildweek-2.description: From the Harry Potter-themed HogTheta challenge to Jangow01 and LupinOne: clues, enumeration and privilege escalation, alongside assessments and testing of web applications and services.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.overview: Black-box challenges are at the heart of this Build Week: analysing lab machines without prior information, connecting clues and reconstructing the path to privileged access. HogTheta brings the investigation into the world of Harry Potter; Jangow01 and LupinOne explore application vulnerabilities, exposed credentials and insecure configurations. The nine documents also cover SQL Injection and XSS in DVWA, Samba and Tomcat assessments, and C code analysis.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.0: Testing SQL Injection and Stored XSS in DVWA, with request analysis using Burp Suite.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.1: Nmap reconnaissance, Nessus vulnerability assessment and lab validation with Metasploit.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.2: The Harry Potter-themed HogTheta, Jangow01 and LupinOne challenges: enumeration, clue analysis and privilege escalation in the lab.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.3: Analysis of C program behaviour, input bounds and buffer overflow cases.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.file.blackbox.1: The Chronicles of HogTheta: challenge walkthrough
buildweeks.buildweek-2.file.code.0: C program analysis and buffer overflow
buildweeks.buildweek-3.title: Malware analysis & traffic investigation
buildweeks.buildweek-3.description: Static and dynamic analysis, PCAP inspection and evidence correlation to reconstruct suspicious activity. A 92-page report collects exercises, further investigations and remediation.
buildweeks.buildweek-3.overview: This Build Week combines AdwereCleaner analysis, assessment of ANY.RUN reports, Linux exercises and investigations into HTTP, HTTPS and DNS traffic. It also includes a Mydoom code review, defensive considerations and two buffer overflow studies in a training environment.
buildweeks.buildweek-3.activity.0: File, hash, process and persistence analysis using dnSpy, Process Monitor and intelligence sources.
buildweeks.buildweek-3.activity.1: Inspection of traffic and files extracted from PCAP with Wireshark, distinguishing transfer evidence from execution evidence.
buildweeks.buildweek-3.activity.2: Correlation of HTTP and DNS events, network sessions and the five-tuple to reconstruct a simulated compromise.
buildweeks.buildweek-3.activity.3: Documentation of indicators, impact assessments and containment and remediation proposals.

buildweeks.challenge.hogtheta.title: HogTheta · Harry Potter
buildweeks.challenge.hogtheta.descriptio: A Harry Potter-themed investigation involving hidden clues, steganography, SQL Injection and port knocking. Two documents describe the paths explored by the team to gain root access: a technical report and the “Chronicles of HogTheta”.
buildweeks.challenge.jangow.title: Jangow01 · From reconnaissance to root
buildweeks.challenge.jangow.description: Reconnaissance and enumeration, discovery of exposed credentials and an RCE vulnerability, followed by analysis of an outdated kernel for privilege escalation.
buildweeks.challenge.lupin.title: LupinOne · Clues and insecure configurations
buildweeks.challenge.lupin.description: Web enumeration and directory fuzzing, recovery of an SSH key, and analysis of insecure permissions and sudo configuration. The report reconstructs the chain of weaknesses leading to root privileges.
